title: In characteristic p a geometrically reduced field extension is separable
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p$ and let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] such that for every field extension $L/k$ the ring $K\otimes_kL$ (the tensor product of [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], with multiplication $(a\otimes\mu)(a'\otimes\mu')=aa'\otimes\mu\mu'$ and unit $1\otimes1$) is reduced (has no nonzero nilpotent elements). Then $K$ is separable over $k$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (2): every subextension $k\subset K'\subset K$ with $K'$ finitely generated as a field over $k$ is separably generated over $k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030W (lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, line 10360), implication (4) => (1), proved in the source as (4) => (3) => (2) => (1) with Lemma Tag 0H71 (lemma-mini-separability, line 10296) for (2) => (1); 'geometrically reduced' (4) is Definition Tag 030S (definition-geometrically-reduced), written out here

proof.text: Let L = ULift (AlgebraicClosure k), lifted to Type (max u v). It is a field extension of k [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-field-extension]. For each coefficient c in k, the polynomial T^p-c has a root in AlgebraicClosure k, since p is positive; lift that root to L. Mathlib IsAlgClosed.exists_pow_nat_eq supplies the proved existence. There is no need to construct the smaller subfield k^{1/p}: the reducedness hypothesis applies to the whole algebraic closure.

source.place: Algebra, paragraph before Lemma Tag 030W (lines 10352-10357): '$k^{1/p}$ ... is the subfield of an algebraic closure of $k$ generated by the $p$th roots of elements of $k$'; the closure of $L$ under the field operations is written out by the agent

proof.text: Apply the hypothesis to L to obtain IsReduced (K tensor_k L). Transport reducedness along Algebra.TensorProduct.comm to A = L tensor_k K [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. The tensor product is nontrivial by Algebra.TensorProduct.nontrivial_of_algebraMap_injective_of_flat_left: L is a nontrivial vector space over k and k maps injectively into K. The algebra map k to A is then injective, so charP_of_injective_algebraMap gives characteristic p.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030W (line 10360): 'The implication (4) => (3) is immediate' (line 10376)

proof.text: Given a finite linearly independent subset s of K and coefficients c with sum c(b) b^p = 0, choose roots r(b) in L with r(b)^p = c(b), from step 1. Put x = sum r(b) tensor b in A. Mathlib sum_pow_char [def-weil-ring-frobenius] and Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_pow give x^p = sum c(b) tensor b^p. Tensor balancing [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] gives x^p = 1 tensor (sum c(b) b^p) = 0.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030W, paragraph 'Assume (3)' (line 10379): 'Consider the ring homomorphism $m:K\otimes_kk^{1/p}\to K$ given by $\lambda\otimes\mu\mapsto\lambda^p\mu^p$. Note that $x^p=m(x)\otimes1$'

proof.text: Reducedness of A gives x = 0. The k-linear independence of s extends to L-linear independence of (1 tensor b) for b in s, directly by the proved Mathlib lemma Module.Flat.linearIndependent_one_tmul, since every vector space over a field is flat [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. Rewriting x as sum r(b) times (1 tensor b), Fintype.linearIndependent_iff gives every r(b) = 0. Raising to p and using injectivity of the algebra map k to L yields every c(b) = 0. Thus p-th powers preserve finite linear independence. No separate basis-extension lemma is needed.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030W, paragraph 'Assume (3)' (lines 10379-10391): 'Since $K\otimes_kk^{1/p}$ is reduced we see $m$ is injective. If $\{a_1,\dots,a_m\}\subset K$ is $k$-linearly independent, then $\{a_1\otimes1,\dots,a_m\otimes1\}$ is $k^{1/p}$-linearly independent. By injectivity of $m$ we deduce that no nontrivial $k$-linear combination of $a_1^p,\dots,a_m^p$ is zero'

proof.text: For any finitely generated intermediate field F of K, IntermediateField.essFiniteType_iff gives Algebra.EssFiniteType k F. The inclusion F.val is injective and k-linear, so finite linear independence passes into K using LinearIndepOn.map_injOn. Apply the p-power independence from step 4 to the finite image set in K; pull it back with LinearIndepOn.comp_of_image and the linear-map criterion. Powers commute with the inclusion. Apply Mathlib exists_isTranscendenceBasis_and_isSeparable_of_linearIndepOn_pow_of_essFiniteType [lem-weil-pbc-p-power-independence-separably-generated] to F to get a finite separating transcendence basis. Its finset coerces to the set required by Algebra.IsSeparablyGenerated. Since F was arbitrary, this proves Algebra.IsSeparableExtension [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030W, paragraph 'Assume (2)' (line 10393): 'To prove (1) we may assume that $K$ is finitely generated over $k$ and we have to prove that $K$ is separably generated over $k$', the rest of the paragraph (minimal inseparability degree and Lemma Tag 0H71, line 10296) being the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-p-power-independence-separably-generated

Five steps: (1) k^{1/p} as {μ in an algebraic closure : μ^p in k}, with unique p-th roots c^{1/p}; (2) (4) => (3) with L = k^{1/p}; (3) the source's x^p = m(x) ⊗ 1, computed for x = Σ b_i ⊗ c_i^{1/p} by the Frobenius of A (the map m itself is not needed); (4) (3) => (2): x^p = (Σ c_i b_i^p) ⊗ 1 = 0 gives x = 0, and the b_i ⊗ 1 are L-independent by extending to a k-basis (lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector) and the basis clause of def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension; (5) (2) => (1): the condition passes to finitely generated subextensions K', and the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-p-power-independence-separably-generated (Mathlib exists_isTranscendenceBasis_and_isSeparable_of_linearIndepOn_pow_of_essFiniteType, tagged 030W (2) => (1) f.g. case, carrying the source's minimal-inseparability argument with 0H71) makes K' separably generated.
